bib.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: All 18 pages (63,307 chars) read, including appendices A-E (E is the theory proof setup; I skimmed its algebra, not verified). Extraction was clean. No embedded instructions.

SOURCE: "ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning". Yanjun Zhao*, Ruizhong Qiu*, Tianxin Wei*, Yuanchen Bei, Zhining Liu, Lingjie Chen, Ismini Lourentzou, Hanghang Tong, Jingrui He (corresponding). All University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Preprint, arXiv:2607.02509v1 [cs.AI], 2 Jul 2026. No venue stated. Code: github.com/Yanjun-Zhao/ReContext.

MAIN CLAIM: Long-context models often fail to use evidence already in the prompt. ReContext is training-free. It scores context tokens by attention from the last w=8 prompt tokens (averaged over selected heads, exponentially decayed). It takes the top-K tokens, copies their containing sentences into an evidence pool, and replays the pool between the full context and the question. It does this for R rounds, with the pool conditioning the next round's scoring. The full context is never pruned ("emphasis, not exclusion"). Main setting: R=2, copied spans taken from the original context only, KV cache reused.

HEADLINE NUMBERS (Table 1; 8 datasets; HELMET 128K versions of NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, PopQA, NarrativeQA, InfBench QA and MC, plus CLIPPER; thinking off; same prompt, decoding and budget per backbone; baselines Vanilla, AttnSharp, DySCO, A-MEM, DAC):
1. Mean Acc across the 8 datasets and 3 backbones (Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Llama3.1-8B): Vanilla 0.24 to ReContext 0.30, "a relative gain of 24.6%".
2. Best average rank on every backbone: 1.00 (Qwen3-4B), 1.46 (Qwen3-8B), 1.29 (Llama3-8B). It does not win every metric. Qwen3-8B loses HotpotQA, InfMC and CLIPPER (CLIPPER 0.33 vs DySCO 0.34).
3. Absolute scores are low for Qwen3-4B. Vanilla NQ Acc is 0.02 and ReContext is 0.08. TriviaQA Acc is 0.04 to 0.30.
4. Cost (CLIPPER, Llama3-8B, 128K): Vanilla 44 min, ReContext 62 min, DySCO 2h13m, A-MEM 50 min. Memory is about the same, since fewer than 128 tokens are added.
Robustness (NQ, PopQA, InfMC only): at 64K the macro-average goes 0.21 to 0.28 (+35.0%). With thinking on (Qwen3-4B) it goes 28.0 to 32.6 (+16.7%). Ablations (Qwen3-4B, per Tables 4, 6, 7 — the model is my inference, not stated): R=1 to R=2 raises the macro-average 0.17 to 0.22. Selecting evidence from the original context only beats the full replay prompt, 0.19 to 0.23.

QUOTES:
- p.1 (Fig. 1): "Top 0.1% of context tokens already accounts for about 50% / 80% accumulated relevance score across three LLMs, corresponding to only 128 tokens in a 128K-token context."
- p.5 (Sec. 4.4): "Averaging the eight Acc columns across all three backbones, RECONTEXT improves over Vanilla from 0.24 to 0.30, a relative gain of 24.6%."

LIMITS:
- Authors concede: it needs access to attention or other internal scores, so it does not work with closed APIs. It adds latency (62 vs 44 min).
- The paper does not show:
  - Any comparison to standard RAG or an external retriever. The baselines are attention rescaling, agentic memory (A-MEM) and compression (DAC).
  - Variance, seeds, confidence intervals, or sample counts per dataset. These are not stated, and the differences are small, often 0.01-0.03.
  - Models larger than 8B, or contexts beyond 128K.
  - Ablations on all datasets. The robustness and ablation tables cover only NQ, PopQA and InfMC, and only on one backbone.
- Theorem 1 (monotonic cosine improvement) rests on an idealized setup of orthogonal token embeddings. It is a stylized argument, not an empirical guarantee.
- Best R and K vary by task. Larger K helps PopQA and InfMC but hurts NQ.
- Baseline scores are very low in places. Qwen3-4B Vanilla has several 0.00-0.04 Acc values, so relative gains are large but absolute gains are small.
- Attention is described as a proposal signal, not a faithful explanation.
- Qualitative evidence is a few inspected cases.

BUILDS ON:
- Lewis et al. 2021 (RAG, arXiv).
- LLMLingua (Jiang et al. 2023) and LongLLMLingua (Jiang et al. 2024).
- DAC (Zhao et al. 2025c).
- A-MEM (Xu et al. 2025).
- DySCO (Ye et al. 2026).
- Query-aware sparsity (Tang et al. 2024).
- SnapKV (Li et al. 2024).
- H2O-style heavy hitters, attention sinks and ScissorHands (Zhang et al. 2023; Xiao et al. 2024; Liu et al. 2023b).
- Lost in the Middle (Liu et al. 2023a).
- SelfElicit (Liu et al. 2025, ACL).
- HELMET (Yen et al. 2025), CLIPPER (Pham et al. 2025).
- Associative memory and Hopfield work (Ramsauer et al. 2021; Krotov et al. 2025; Nichani et al. 2025; Olsson et al. 2022).

NOTE FOR 04-retrieval.md: this is an internal-attention evidence-replay method, not retrieval over an external index. It fits as a "retrieve within the prompt" or harness idea, and as a contrast with RAG and compression.
